requirements.text: Seats: long- and short-lived, state card, template copy then tune, seat management page with worker activity, user layer vs lead layer.

Instances and the instance page: per-instance home; gogoke-managed, fixed official CLI installation, explicit upgrade, rollback, doctor, update check and zero-instance uninstall without reading user global npm; login, display name, enablement, concurrency, seat/session counts, model and source-backed account/subscription/error/expiry/recovery/abnormal-close states; no quota integration or model-spending probe in v1.
Sessions are cache, seat ledger is the sole authority; restart reconciliation; native resume/fork only as equivalent optimisations.
Side chat window: fork lead context by ledger position, batched sync, on-demand read of this project's threads, keep/archive/delete, may write within its permission tier.
Inbox: queue, steer, cancel, edit; interrupt-and-resume fallback disclosed.
Secretary as a global seat: real-time read of all projects' threads, delivery to leads and auditors, resident and scheduled triggers, per-project filtering on distribution.
Lead orchestrates subordinate seats inside user-set bounds; cannot change its own instance; no recursive seat creation; parallel cap from machine resources.
Isolated write spaces; permission tiers enforced by the host with the mechanisms actually available, stated honestly; main tree written only through merge by a permitted seat.

Five CLIs in v1: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, each installed by gogoke from a verified fixed official version and reported with its measured capabilities; B5 unsupported account isolation is not promoted by installation.
Configurable call-permission table enforced by the host; forged or unauthorised senders rejected; subordinate seats cannot reach the Owner.
Gate and stage primitives: approve or reject with reason, reject cap then escalate, user-defined stages, configured gates cannot be bypassed, every transition recorded.
Configurable escalation chain executed by the host; stuck or stalled seats escalate automatically.
Formal review sessions are zero-inheritance; Owner side-chat talk never enters delegated review; workers cannot see Owner-lead conversation.
Global context and memory are unreachable from project-scope retrieval; distribution into a project is explicit, filtered and cited.
Every question to the Owner carries proposed solutions and a free answer; vendor-native question cards shown as-is, otherwise ours; answers are bound back to the asking turn.
Lead answers the takeover questions, including how the project space works, before it may dispatch; each answer cites a source or says unknown and how to find out.
All worktrees created by the host under one standard outside the repository; single and mixed trees stored apart; relations kept as a graph; vendor-native worktree creation not used.
Each instance has its own home, separate from the Owner's everyday CLI homes, with vendor memory turned off; explicit child environment.
Health signals drive automatic compaction and session renewal with a low-key record; instance changes stay explicit.
A repository may serve several projects; commits carry project, seat, instance and turn identity; push credentials are never read or copied by the host.
Cross-line contracts are frozen before parallel work; fakes and real implementations pass the same contract tests; stored records stay readable across schema changes.
Queued: steer, edit, cancel; recipient never changes on focus change.
Steering: shows inserting; never delivered without a receipt.
Steer hit turn end: stays queued or cancel; never silently moved to the next turn or another seat.
Delivered: time shown, interrupt-and-resume disclosed; no recall or edit.
Delivery unknown: read-only check, no automatic resend.
Cancelled: struck through, record kept.
Failed: requeue creates a new message and keeps the old one.
Idle: dispatch, change instance, reclaim, short to long; lead only touches lead-layer seats inside bounds.
Working: inbox and steer, request stop; no instance change while busy.
Switching instance: reason shown; never dispatch to old and new sessions at once.
Stop requested: shown until the stop fact arrives; no new work into an overlapping workspace before it, including leftover child processes and restarts.
Stuck or stalled: escalates along the configured chain; no Owner popup unless the chain reaches the Owner.
Reclaiming: the lead's own reclaim conditions are checked; reclaim refused when unmet.
Reclaimed: greyed out, ledger kept and readable.
New side chat: seat and instance chosen, ledger position and permission tier shown; no model call before the first question.
Active: ask, read this project's threads, inbox operations, writes only within the permission tier; never another project; synced content never executed.
Lead progressed: pending deltas shown and attached to the next question, or appended where the vendor supports append without a turn; no model call for syncing.
Kept by default: resumable; forked lead context not duplicated.
Archived: restore or delete.
Deleted: only the side chat's own content removed; lead ledger unchanged.
Not installed: gogoke offers installation of its pinned official CLI into its own managed root, with verified source and bytes; no user global npm or PATH lookup.
Installed, not logged in: the Owner logs in inside the CLI; the host never reads or copies credential files.

Logged in: concurrency cap set and enforced; masked account and subscription, source-backed OpenCode credential origin, seats served and active session count, selected model and abnormal-close records shown when evidenced; unknown fields remain unknown, and quota view or model-spending probe is not in v1.
New version: show a source-backed notice; the User explicitly requests host-managed upgrade or rollback, never automatic switching; active or UNKNOWN holder/session refuses version change.

Exhausted or error: show the CLI original reason, affected seats, expiry and recovery time only when directly evidenced; a detected wrong account is not adopted; no silent instance change or model-spending quota probe.

shared_files.conditional_rule: A conditional file is recorded in T00 or L0 as either MODIFIED, with the change, or VERIFIED_UNCHANGED, with the reason; no line widens its own scope to reach it.

contracts.rule: Frozen in L0. Each operation fixes request and receipt, trusted caller, permission and version checks, state transitions, idempotency, race and recovery semantics, and which store owns the durable state. Fakes and real implementations run the same contract tests. real_stage is the milestone at which the real implementation is settled; every contract is settled again on the candidate at M3. Changing a frozen contract is a change request.

operations.seams: B emits vendor-raw events tagged with session; A normalises. E asks for compact and renew through this contract and receives capability-insufficient or failure receipts with the old and new generation; E never builds vendor-private commands. Admission is one boundary for E's cap, F's concurrency and H's launch. A remains the sole session-purpose authority. H derives continuation from original observed replies, confirmed STOPPED episodes and current bindings. A verified continuation may reuse its F-owned private history directory across generations; a new native session starts empty, formal continuation remains refused, and existing history is preserved without guessing ownership. Legacy ACL recovery preserves the immutable original fence, schema, boot_identity and captured custody pairs on the original physical database, registered root/home and credential object. Authority requires every exact fenced PID/creation_time_100ns to be gone and a directly queried kernel boot-start FILETIME strictly later than every fenced creation time, plus unchanged original identities and settled unlisted/current holders and intents. At each begin, prewrite and finish, the original custody pairs are rechecked against the fence and the same boot-start value and holder states are reobserved under the existing revision CAS and two-step ACL journal. A BCD BootIdentifier is retained only as old metadata, never as proof; new boot metadata, if needed, uses boot-start:<16hexFILETIME> and string inequality grants nothing. Missing/changed fence, failed or uncertain process query, live exact holder, insufficient boot-start time, unknown links, replaced roots/objects and unlisted UNKNOWN refuse with original errors. Original UNKNOWN/NULL stop proof, continuation STOPPED requirement, committed reservations and worktree cleanup remain unchanged. No credential content access, CLI/capability/home change, automatic reboot or new login; partial ACL work is reconciled by metadata before model launch. Native boot query failure retains original NTSTATUS. This is one detail revision: if the real legacy root still cannot recover cleanly, stop this path, preserve the original state, report first, then join new-instance login to the existing OT4b Owner touchpoint. The independent fence, with direct exact-holder-gone and boot-start-after-every-old-creation proof, separately authorizes exact legacy grant migration and exact unprotected source baseline DACL preparation under the existing Owner/SYSTEM/Administrators policy, only for the unchanged original single-link credential object without aliases, with complete captured old holder/ACL provenance and no unlisted or current holder/intent. The existing E.2 caller authorizes the existing merge operation and reason. A seat edits files only inside its authorized host-created worktree; it does not run Git or access .git. Under the original F physical worktree/repository binding, original H StopFact, and no active admission reservation, F uses the Owner-registered exact Git pin to create a local child commit carrying project, seat, instance, and authorizing native-turn identity, then performs the existing source merge while preserving the clean-source requirement. Persist the child-seal intent under and bound to the original MERGE request before that effect, then retain the original child commit hash receipt. If the child commit occurred but merge or database receipt completion is uncertain, retain MERGE_UNKNOWN and refuse replay through either the original or a new request. Every read model and action maps to an operation of the contracts above with its receipt; G adds no operation or state source of its own; every A1-A4 state has a read model, including unknown and unconfirmed states. At M1 with G.0: instance read models for the four states not installed, not logged in, logged in and error (including a failed login's raw reason), and the login start, progress, result and cancel actions; at M2, the managed CLI/version and source-backed exhaustion read models settle with F.2 and V13; the remaining instance management presentation settles at M3. The CLI read model distinguishes operation status/progress/original failure, current version, verified new version, unverified official new-version notice, previous verified version and last check time. The instance read model may expose display name, enabled state, last-confirmed masked account/subscription and OpenCode source, current login-status detection error, recent records, seats and active session count, cap, selected model and separately evidenced available models, expiry, explicit CLI recovery time, masked wrong-account-not-adopted and abnormal-close records only from the responsible host observations. Missing or ambiguous values stay UNKNOWN, and no model call is made to measure quota. The detect control only requests non-spending login status; doctor has its own control and result and is never used as detect. Upgrade and rollback run only after an explicit User click, but the host downloads, verifies and installs the bytes without any manual CLI download or installation by the Owner. UI actions are gated by host capability: create immediately starts supported login-only, rename, enable/disable, delete with in-use refusal, cap, detect and open the controlled home; unsupported actions are hidden. Writes land only in host-created worktrees; a direct write to the main tree is refused; a vendor-native worktree attempt outside the space is blocked; a read-only or no-network tier the host cannot guarantee is refused or shown as unavailable, never passed on a weaker statement; single and mixed trees stored apart, including one repository serving two projects; the graph answers origin, users and merge target; merge only by the existing permitted-seat authorization with reason recorded; the seat edits files only in the host-created worktree and neither runs Git nor accesses .git; after the original H StopFact and no-active-reservation gate, F seals the stopped child change with project, seat, instance and authorizing native-turn identity before the existing merge, and reads back the seal intent plus exact child commit hash bound to the original MERGE request; a child commit followed by uncertain merge/receipt remains UNKNOWN and cannot be repeated by old or new request; push credentials never read.

evidence_carryover.rule: Every check result is bound to the source commit and the hashes of the components it exercised. V16 publishes the per-check provenance table.

Testing: the backbone is a repeatable end-to-end run on the Owner's Win11 against the installed candidate and the real test instances, at each stable point; per-CLI golden protocol transcripts are the adapters' regression base and are re-recorded on CLI upgrade; unit and compiled-mutation tests are kept for security boundaries (isolation, permissions, credentials, signing chain), not added for every change.

Checkpoints within a stage record what changed, the result, the next step, the precedents and the raw failure text; full hashes, receipts and artifact ids are compiled at stable points and acceptance.

authorization.binding: The receipt records the scope digest that verify_plan.py computes from PLAN.json (requirements, lines with write scopes and dependencies, milestone ids, conditional shared-file ownership and paths, durable contract ownership, invariants, Owner touchpoints, governance, authorization, non-claims). Construction and the candidate signer check that the plan in force has that digest. The S1-R4 authorization does not cover this plan and is not modified.
authorization.amendment_rule: An amendment that leaves the scope digest unchanged changes only details (phase placement and milestone notes, deliverable, contract and check descriptions, assets, source pins); it never widens write scope, adds a shared file, changes contract ownership or a recorded Owner decision. Independent review must preserve requirements, invariants and security. It takes effect when an independent audit passes and the Controller merges the plan PR; no new receipt and no Owner merge. An amendment that changes the scope digest carries the updated receipt in the same PR, and the Owner merges that one PR.
authorization.governance_note: This follows the S1-R4 authorization pattern at a separate path, bound to scope instead of plan bytes. Merging this plan is the Owner's acceptance of that pattern for design 37.

scope_nonclaims: This plan proves no code, cloud run, installer or Owner-machine result.
evidence REAL is a declaration of where a check must be settled; the verifier cannot confirm evidence.
Fakes serve parallel development and contract tests only; no check passes on a fake.
Second batch is out of scope: decision register, quota, long-term memory.
Usage is out of scope: role counts, merge-permission holders, flows.
